session.title: Operating Systems Revision
session.subject: Computer Science
session.summary:
## Revision Guide: Computer Science

### Executive Overview
Operating Systems: Process Synchronization and Deadlocks
Mutual Exclusion: Only one process can enter the critical section at any time.

### Core Concepts & Pillars
- **Operating Systems**: Process Synchronization and Deadlocks
- **Mutual Exclusion**: Only one process can enter the critical section at any time.
- **Hold and Wait**: Process holds resources while requesting additional ones.
- **No Preemption**: Resources cannot be forcibly taken away from processes.
- **Circular Wait**: A closed chain of processes each waiting for resource held by next.

### Key Mechanisms & Principles
1. No Preemption: Resources cannot be forcibly taken away from processes.
1. Circular Wait: A closed chain of processes each waiting for resource held by next.
1. Banker's Algorithm: An avoidance technique developed by Dijkstra to evaluate safe states.

> **Exam Tip**: Pay special attention to distinguishing definitions and boundary cases during quizzes.
